_readme: Walks around Hollowmere (js/events/walks.js, samWalk). Placeholders depend on the section.

goddess: pre-binding disguise encounters and post-binding strolls. Placeholders: {alias}, {form}, {race}, {house}, {sam}, {goddess}. Pre-binding choices with resIn can trigger evGoddessDistract via gDistractAct (she never lets Sam finish).
casual: encounters with randomly generated NPCs (buffs Sam's Technique). Placeholders: {name}, {race}, {act}, {job}, {house}.
casualRecruit: follow-up when Sam's Technique meets walk.casual.recruitTech after a casual encounter. Placeholders: {name}, {race}, {house}.

partnerIntros: meeting an unchosen partner on a walk, one entry per partner key: open (where you see her; its own page, also shown before the NG++ memory lines, so keep it neutral), story (the meeting and her pitch, shown with the hire choices), hire (result when she joins), image {comp, setting, sam} (comp = pose only). They tell the same meeting as data/goddess/partner-intros.json (the starter-partner version); keep the two in step. Once she has been recruited in an earlier cycle (NG++), partnerMemoryLines / partnerMemoryHire [3 tiers by how often she has come back] replace story / hire. Placeholders: {name}, {first}, {house}, {loc}, {goddess}.

events: rest / coin / flavor walk events (type: 'rest' | 'coin' | 'flavor'). Choices declare declarative effects (energy, gold, rep, sam, appXP, mood (everyone at Sam's house), workerMood/workerTrust (needWorker's {lady}), outfitDiscount, regularLoyalty) and optional stat check (check: {stat, label, need, win, lose}).
Folder: base.json (this file) holds every section except the partner ones; partners.json holds partnerIntros, partnerMemoryLines and partnerMemoryHire (one entry per partner key in each).

disguise.title: A Familiar Face in the Crowd
disguise.intro:
Lanternlight catches the gold tips of long black hair three stalls ahead of you in the afternoon market. Before you can look away, {form} steps neatly out of the crowd and falls into step beside you.

"{alias}," she says brightly, linking her arm through yours as though you'd arranged to meet here. "You walk too fast, {sam}. You're going to miss everything worth looking at."
disguise.wonder:
Her palm is startlingly warm through your sleeve. You try to place her—not one of your staff, and certainly not any townswoman you remember—until she leans in close enough for you to smell faint candle smoke and warm honey.

"Looking for someone?" {alias} asks, her eyes bright with amusement.

image.comp: walking arm in arm through a sunlit market street, looking up at him with a teasing smile, hand tucked around his elbow
image.setting: busy cobblestone market street with colorful stalls and hanging paper lanterns

choices.label: "Who told you my name?"
choices.resIn: "Everyone in the Lantern Quarter talks, darling," she murmurs, backing you into the quiet alcove between two spice stalls with her palm flat over your fly. "Come here. Let me keep your hands busy so you stop thinking."
choices.res: "A little bird," she says, tapping the tip of your nose while her free hand gives your cock a bold, shameless squeeze through your trousers. By the time you blink past the scent of cinnamon and candle smoke, she has slipped into the crowd and left you aching.

choices.label: Walk with her awhile
choices.resIn: You let her lead the pace down a narrow lane behind the silk stalls. The moment nobody is looking, she pushes you against the brick and goes straight for your belt.
choices.res: You stroll the stalls with her for half an hour, trading dry remarks about the merchants while her fingers brush dangerously close to your groin every time nobody looks. When you turn to buy roasted chestnuts, the cobblestones beside you are empty.

disguise.title: At the Canal Rail
disguise.intro:
Halfway across the canal bridge, {form} is leaning over the stone parapet, watching paper boats drift beneath the arches. She glances over her shoulder as your boots hit the cobbles—black hair tipped with gold catching the late sun.

"Fancy meeting you here," {alias} purrs, patting the warm stone beside her. "Take a break. The ledger won't catch fire if you look at the river for five minutes."
disguise.wonder: You lean on the parapet beside her. Within a minute she has pressed her bare hip tight against yours, her palm sliding brazenly over your trousers to trace your growing bulge as if you weren't standing in broad daylight. Something in the effortless way she claims your space makes your pulse hammer.

image.comp: leaning against a stone canal bridge beside him, looking sideways with a sly smile, hair blowing softly in the breeze
image.setting: stone bridge over a quiet canal in warm late-afternoon light

choices.label: Ask where she's staying
choices.resIn: "Closer than you think," she whispers, steering you down into the deep shadow beneath the bridge steps with her fingers already hooking into your waistband.
choices.res: "Somewhere with a great view of {house}," she says lightly, kissing the corner of your mouth after one last slow stroke through your trousers, then slipping down the stairs before you catch your breath.

choices.res: She stays until the canal lamps flicker on, resting her chin on your shoulder with one warm palm resting unrepentantly over your thighs before vanishing as a barge passes.

disguise.title: Candle Smoke at the Crossroads
disguise.intro:
A step off the main road sits an old roadside lantern shrine, mossy and quiet. Standing before the unlit brass bowl is {form}—though when she turns, you already know that gold-tipped black hair and those impossible lamp-bright eyes.

"{goddess}," you say flatly. She laughs, delighted, and snaps her fingers so the shrine wick catches with a soft pop.
disguise.wonder: "Spoilsport," she says, strolling straight up until her breasts press against your chest and her fingers hook into your belt. "Out shopping for trouble without me? Play along as {alias} if you know what's good for you—and remember the rule: you still don't get to cum."

image.comp: standing beside an old stone lantern shrine, smiling smugly with one finger brushing his collar, small ember light glowing nearby
image.setting: quiet mossy roadside shrine shaded by trees, warm dusk light

choices.label: Call her bluff and pull her behind the shrine
choices.resIn: "Oh, bold today, {sam}," {goddess} purrs, already unbuckling your trousers as she backs you behind the stone shrine.
choices.res: "Impatient," she chides softly, wrapping her fingers around your bare cock to stroke you right to the brink against the shrine stone—and vanishing in a swirl of warm candle smoke the heartbeat before you cum.

choices.res: "I never slack off, stranger," {alias} replies with a crooked, smug grin, pinching your ass as she walks you halfway back to {house} before fading down a side alley.

disguise.title: Out of the Rain
disguise.intro:
A sudden drizzle drives you under a narrow tavern awning, shaking water from your hoodie—only to find {form} already waiting there, completely dry despite the rain drumming on the street.

"You're soaked," {alias} notes, though her glowing gold eyes have already dropped straight to your groin. You catch that smug little smile and realize the air under the awning smells like warm wax and candle sparks.
disguise.wonder: {goddess} steps right inside your open coat, her warm palms sliding under your shirt and straight down to cup your cock through your damp trousers. "Nobody can see past the rain," she murmurs against your jaw. "So don't waste it asking dumb questions."

image.comp: standing close under a wooden awning while rain falls behind them, drying his collar with a mischievous grin
image.setting: lantern-lit cobblestone street during a light rain shower, wooden awning

choices.label: Press her against the wall and tell her to prove it
choices.resIn: "Say please, {sam}," {goddess} murmurs, parting the front of your trousers with both hands while the rain curtains off the alley behind you.
choices.res: "I wanted to remind you whose hands feel best," she whispers shamelessly, pumping your cock hard right through your fly until your hips buck—then kissing your jaw and stepping dryly into the downpour, leaving you throbbing and high and dry.

choices.label: Wait out the rain with her
choices.res: She leans shamelessly against your chest until the clouds break, drying your shirt with the heat off her bronze skin while her fingertips tap idle, teasing circles over your belt.

bound.title: Out in Disguise
bound.text:
Halfway down the market street, {form} slips smoothly into step beside you and laces her fingers through yours. You only need one glance at the gold tips of her hair and that smug sidelong grin to recognize {goddess}.

"Couldn't stand watching you stroll around town by yourself," she whispers, leaning her tits into your arm. "Come on. Buy me something sweet, pretend I'm a stranger, and let's see where you drag me afterwards."

image.comp: walking hand in hand through a busy street looking fondly at him, wearing a playful disguise
image.setting: warm afternoon market street with lanterns

choices.label: Buy her honey pastries (-20g)
choices.res: {goddess} eats both pastries with obvious delight and licks honey off her thumb just to watch you stare. "Good mortal. Wait until tonight."

choices.label: Play along with the stranger act
choices.res: You introduce yourself as if for the first time, and she plays coy all the way back to {house}—slipping her hand over your cock in every dark doorway just to make you swear.

bound.title: A Quiet Detour
bound.text: On the canal bridge, a familiar voice calls out from a bench—{goddess}, wearing {form} like a favorite coat, swinging her legs above the water. "Your ladies have the house covered for an hour," she tells you, patting the bench beside her with glowing gold eyes. "Sit. You look like you could use me."

image.comp: sitting on a stone bridge bench swinging her legs, beckoning him with an affectionate smile
image.setting: quiet canal bridge at dusk, warm lantern reflection on water

choices.label: Rest your head in her lap
choices.res: She laughs softly and cards warm fingers through your hair while your cheek rests against her bare thigh until the sky turns deep violet. You head back strangely rested.

choices.label: Tease her about sneaking out
choices.res: "Goddesses don't sneak, {sam}," she replies primly, squeezing your knee with warm fingers. "I was checking up on what's mine."

casual.title: Caught in the Rain
casual.setting: quiet cobblestone archway sheltered from a warm afternoon downpour
casual.text:
A sudden downpour chases you under a narrow stone archway—already occupied by {name}, a friendly {race} shaking rain from her hair. The two of you stand shoulder to shoulder watching the gutters flood, trading dry jokes until her gaze drops to your mouth and doesn't come back up.

"Looks like we're stuck here for a bit," she murmurs, stepping inside your coat out of the chill. "Might as well keep each other busy."
casual.goRes: Sheltered behind the archway's stone pillar, wet clothes are shoved aside fast. She gasps into your mouth while your hands work over her bare skin, and hers waste no time dropping straight to your cock until both of you are flushed, sticky, and breathless when the rain breaks.
casual.passRes: You keep your hands to yourself and chat easily until the rain slows. She waves warmly as you step back into the street.

casual.title: Upstairs at the Tavern
casual.setting: quiet sunlit upstairs room above a neighborhood tavern, narrow bed
casual.text:
At a quiet neighborhood tavern, you end up sharing a corner table with {name}, a bright-eyed {race} traveling through town. One drink turns into two, easy laughter turning warm and unhurried. When she taps her empty cup and glances toward the innkeeper's stairs, there's nothing subtle about her smile.

"My room's paid through tonight," {name} says softly, brushing your knee under the table. "Come up for an hour and show me what you've got?"
casual.goRes: The latch clicks behind you, clothes hit the floorboards, and she pulls you bare onto the narrow mattress. Unhurried and loud when she likes what you're doing, she takes everything you give her until the bedframe is knocking and neither of you is rushing back downstairs.
casual.passRes: You raise your cup to her instead and keep the afternoon light. She laughs, pays her tab, and heads off down the road.

casual.title: The Quiet Boathouse
casual.setting: dim wooden canal boathouse smelling of cedar and river breeze
casual.text:
Along the quiet lower canal, you strike up a conversation with {name}, a {race} watching the barges drift by with boredom in her posture and sparks in her eyes. Ten minutes of easy flirting later, she unlocks the little cedar boathouse behind her aunt's shop and jerks her chin inside.

"Nobody comes down here till dusk," she grins, pulling the door half-shut behind you.
casual.goRes: Among coiled ropes and sunlit dust, she pushes your trousers straight down against the cedar workbench and gets right to work—mouth, hands, and body eager until both of you are sweating through your shirts and grinning like thieves.
casual.passRes: You laugh and beg off for today, leaving her lounging in the doorway with an amused wave.

casual.title: After-Hours Tea
casual.setting: warm candlelit backroom behind an apothecary shop, shelves of dried herbs
casual.text:
You stop by a quiet backstreet apothecary to pick up salves, where {name}—a {race} closing up for the afternoon—offers you spiced tea in the backroom instead. Halfway through the pot, she stretches with a groan about her stiff shoulders, then looks right at you from under her lashes.

"You look like someone who knows what he's doing with his hands," she purrs, slipping her outer wrap off bare shoulders.
casual.goRes: The shop bell stays unhung while your oiled palms work the knots out of her back and shoulders—then slide over her bare tits and hips when she arches into you and pulls you out of your trousers. By the time she lets you dress, she is flushed from collarbone to thighs.
casual.passLabel: Finish your tea and head out
casual.passRes: You finish the spiced tea, thank her for the salves, and leave her humming cheerfully behind the counter.

casual.title: Behind the Ivy Wall
casual.setting: secluded stone bench tucked behind an ivy-covered courtyard wall at dusk
casual.text:
Taking a shortcut past an overgrown courtyard, you nearly walk straight into {name}, a charming {race} sitting alone on a stone bench behind the ivy wall. What starts as an apology turns into twenty minutes of teasing banter—until she tugs you down beside her by the front of your hoodie.

"Nobody walks past here this late," she whispers against your jaw. "Want to see how quiet I can be?"
casual.goRes: Hidden behind the thick ivy, she tugs your trousers open and bites her lip to muffle every sharp gasp while you touch, kiss, and fuck the breath right out of her against the warm stone.
casual.passRes: You smile, squeeze her hand, and slip back out onto the lane before dark.

casualRecruit.title: Second Thoughts: {name}
casualRecruit.text:
You are halfway to fastening your clothes when {name} catches your wrist, still catching her breath and looking at you with wide, freshly appreciative eyes.

"Wait a second," she says, letting out a breathless laugh as she pushes damp hair back from her face. "Where did you learn how to use your hands like that? You mentioned running {house}—were you actually looking for someone new, or do you just leave people half-ruined in alleys for fun?"
casualRecruit.hireRes: {name} grins, pulls her clothes straight, and falls into step beside you back toward {house}. "If the rest of the staff gets treated half that well, I'm in."
casualRecruit.candRes: {name} tucks the address of {house} into her sleeve with a slow, wicked smile. "Give me a day to pack my things. Expect me."
casualRecruit.passLabel: Keep things casual and wish her well
casualRecruit.passRes: "Fair enough," {name} laughs, kissing your cheek before slipping away down the lane. "If I ever pass through again, I know where to find you."

casualPaid: As you fasten your trousers, {name} presses {gold} into your palm with a brisk, satisfied pat on your cheek and a warm "Keep the change, handsome," leaving you standing alone on the flagstones wondering which one of you just worked a shift.

Before you have even caught your breath, {name} fixes her hair, slips {gold} straight into your hoodie pocket with an amused wink, and disappears back into the street—leaving you staring at the coins, oddly paid and faintly used.

"Good hands," {name} murmurs lazily, tucking her blouse back in and counting {gold} onto the edge beside your knee before strolling away without another word. You pocket the money anyway, though you feel suspiciously like the hired talent for once.
guestIntro: Passing the fountain plaza, you notice someone who plainly doesn't belong to Hollowmere's usual crowd—{name}. {backstory}

events.title: The Quiet Shrine Bench
events.text: Down a shaded lane behind the old lantern shrine, you find a sun-warmed stone bench where nobody passes for an hour. The breeze smells of pine and warm dust, and your shoulders drop an inch the moment you sit.

choices.label: Close your eyes for half an hour
choices.res: You doze with your back against the warm stone and wake with a clear head and steady legs.

choices.label: Leave an offering at the shrine (-15g)
choices.res: The caretaker beams, hands you a cup of sweet herbal tea, and tells three passing merchants what a decent fellow runs the house down the hill.

events.title: The Harbor Tea Stall
events.text: Above the harbor steps, an elderly dwarf runs a tiny wooden tea cart overlooking the sails. Steam rises from spiced kettles while gulls wheel lazily overhead.

choices.label: Buy hot tea and steamed buns (-20g)
choices.res: Hot ginger tea and fluffy pork buns bring the life right back into your bones.

choices.label: Sit on the low wall and chat
choices.res: The old dwarf pours you a free splash from the end of the pot and trades dockyard gossip until your legs feel light again.

events.title: Breeze by the Canal
events.text: On the grassy bank past the upper canal lock, willows trail in the slow current and a warm breeze keeps the afternoon noise at bay.

choices.label: Stretch out in the grass and rest
choices.res: Half an hour staring at clouds through willow leaves clears the ledger haze straight out of your head.

choices.label: Watch the barge traffic and take notes
choices.res: Watching merchants, dockers, and off-duty guards pass sharpens your eye for who has coin to spend.

events.title: The Tangled Tariff
events.text: Outside the merchant gate, a harried caravan clerk is surrounded by three fluttering stacks of customs parchment, muttering numbers under his breath while his inkwell tips dangerously close to his sleeve.

choices.label: Sort out his ledger for him

win.res: Ten minutes with a borrowed pen untangles an entire column of double-counted wool tariffs. He presses {gold} into your palm in pure relief.

lose.res: You spot two arithmetic errors before your eyes cross—still enough to earn a grateful {gold} finder's tip.

choices.label: Point him toward your house for a drink tonight
choices.res: He gratefully pockets a card for {house} and promises to stop by with his caravan mates tonight.

events.title: Alley Cups
events.text: Near the dockside steps, a fast-talking hustler flips three tarnished brass cups across an upturned barrel while two bored sailors watch. "Double your stake if you track the pearl, friend!"

choices.label: Play his game and watch his wrists

win.res: His left thumb gave it away before the second pass. You scoop up {gold} before he decides he's suddenly out of change.

lose.res: Too fast. You drop 15g, though you catch the trick the moment he pockets the cups.

choices.label: Watch silently from the steps
choices.res: You stand back with your hands in your pockets and study how he reads marks in the crowd.

events.title: A Broken Cart Axle
events.text: A baker's cart has snapped an axle halfway up the cobblestone hill, blocking half the lane with heavy grain sacks while the owner tries fruitlessly to flag down help.

choices.label: Haul the sacks up to his shop

win.res: It leaves your hoodie dusty and your arms burning, yet every sack makes it inside before the drizzle starts. He presses {gold} on you and insists you take a loaf.

lose.res: It takes twice as many trips as you expected, earning {gold} and a sore lower back.

choices.label: Hire two dockhands to help and direct traffic (-20g)
choices.res: The lane clears in five minutes, and half the street hears that the owner of {house} stepped up to sort it out.

events.title: The Traveling Peddler's Trunk
events.text: At the edge of the square, a sunburned clothier is packing down a cedar trunk stuffed with bright silks, neatly pressed dresses, and bolted lace he wants moved before sundown.

choices.label: Buy an outfit for the house wardrobe at clearance
choices.res: You pick out {outfit} at a steep discount ({cost}) and have it sent straight to the wardrobe at {house}.

choices.label: Help him price and move the remaining bolts

win.res: You steer three passing seamstresses straight to his bolts and earn a modest {gold} commission.

lose.res: You drum up a couple of small buyers and pocket {gold} for the trouble.

events.title: Corner Lute & Crowd
events.text: A sharp-tongued young bard has drawn two dozen off-duty merchants and adventurers around the fountain plaza, singing bright, bawdy tavern ballads.

choices.label: Toss a coin and buy a verse about {house} (-25g)
choices.res: The bard grins, switches keys without blinking, and weaves {house}'s lanterns neatly into the chorus. Half the crowd looks up the street.

choices.label: Work the edge of the crowd

win.res: Easy banter leaves four well-dressed merchants asking what time your doors open tonight.

lose.res: You hand out a couple of polite words before the song wraps up and the crowd scatters.

events.title: The Old Bookseller's Cart
events.text: Tucked beside the clocktower wall sits a rickety cart piled high with dog-eared manuals—half merchant ledgers, half anatomical sketches and pillow-books.

choices.label: Buy a worn technique treatise (-70g)
choices.res: You thumb through a surprisingly practical volume on breath, pace, and hands over a bench in the square. Useful.

choices.label: Browse the market almanacs and chat
choices.res: The old bookseller lets you skim his town registries for free while complaining about rising parchment prices.

events.title: Cornered by the Bakery
events.text: Rounding a narrow corner, you spot two drunken brawlers blocking a terrified apprentice tailor against a wall, reaching for his delivery satchel.

choices.label: Step between them and back them off

win.res: Your tone—and the unexpected solidity behind it—convince them to find an easier street. The tailor presses {gold} on you in thanks.

lose.res: You take a bruised rib pulling the kid clear before the watch whistle sounds down the block.

choices.label: Bluff that the city watch captain is right behind you

win.res: They bolt down the side lane before checking the corner. The tailor thanks you breathless and hands over {gold}.

lose.res: They glare, hesitate just long enough for the tailor to bolt past, and slink off cursing.

events.title: A Familiar Patron
events.text: Outside a corner coffee stall, you nearly walk straight into {regular}—who looks far less composed in broad daylight when he realizes it's you, hastily straightening his collar.

choices.label: Buy him a quiet cup and keep his secret (-20g)
choices.res: He relaxes over coffee, clearly relieved you didn't announce his favorite house to the street. "See you Friday, Takahashi."

choices.label: Mention tonight's lineup with a grin
choices.res: His eyes light up at once; by the time you part ways, he's already rearranging his evening plans.

events.title: Off the Clock
events.text: Halfway down Ribbon Lane, you spot {lady} squinting critically at a display of ribbons and glass hairpins. She catches sight of you and perks up at once.

choices.label: Buy her a ribbon and sweet cake (-30g)
choices.res: {lady} lights up, slipping the ribbon straight into her sleeve before walking the rest of the square beside you.

choices.label: Stroll back to {house} together
choices.res: The walk home passes twice as fast with {lady} trading idle remarks about every shop window on the street.

events.title: Caught in the Rain
events.text: The sky over Hollowmere opens without warning. You duck under a cobbler's awning and find yourself shoulder to shoulder with a flower seller, a soaked priest and a cat that clearly owns the place.

choices.label: Wait it out and listen to the gossip
choices.res: By the time the rain eases you know which baker is courting which widow, what the priest really thinks of the bishop, and that the cat is called Magistrate.

choices.label: Buy the flower seller's last bunch for {house} (-15g)
choices.res: You walk home damp and smelling of violets. The bunch ends up in a chipped jug on the front counter, and three clients ask about it.

events.title: Chess by the Fountain
events.text: An old man with a waxed moustache sits at a fold-out board by the fountain, a sign propped against his stool: BEAT ME, WIN A COPPER. LOSE, BUY ME TEA.

choices.label: Sit down and play

win.res: You win in thirty-one moves. He laughs, pays his copper, and makes you promise a rematch next week.

lose.res: He takes your queen with a pawn and the most smug sip of tea you've ever seen. You buy the tea.

choices.label: Watch a game and move on
choices.res: You watch him dismantle a cocky student in twelve moves. It's oddly restful.

events.title: Lanterns on Ribbon Lane
events.text: Shopkeepers on Ribbon Lane are stringing paper lanterns between the eaves for some saint's day nobody can quite name. A ladder wobbles. Someone shouts for an extra pair of hands.

choices.label: Hold the ladder and hang a few
choices.res: An hour later the lane glows orange and the shopkeepers know your name and your house. One of them winks when he says it.

choices.label: Buy a lantern for {house} (-20g)
choices.res: The paper lantern gets hung over the front door. The ladies argue for a while about whether it's tacky, then all of them light it.

events.title: On the Temple Steps
events.text: A young acolyte is sweeping the temple steps and very carefully not looking at you. You realize he knows exactly who you are and what you run.

choices.label: Say good morning anyway
choices.res: He goes red, mumbles a blessing, and then, after a pause, asks whether the ladies are well. You tell him they are. He looks relieved.

choices.label: Drop a donation in the box (-25g)
choices.res: The coins clink. The acolyte stops pretending not to see you and bows, a little stiffly. Word gets around that the Lantern's owner tithes.

events.title: The Skewer Stall
events.text: Smoke and garlic drift from a skewer stall by the river bridge. The cook flips meat over a coal brazier and shouts prices nobody listens to.

choices.label: Eat standing by the river (-6g)
choices.res: Charred, salty, too hot to hold. You eat three and watch the barges go by until your feet stop aching.

choices.label: Bring a bag home for the ladies (-30g)
choices.res: The bag doesn't survive the front hall. Somebody fights somebody else for the last skewer, and everyone is in a better mood for it.

events.title: Lost in the Market
events.text: A little boy is standing in the middle of the fish market, very still, trying not to cry. Everyone is stepping around him.

choices.label: Help him find his mother
choices.res: It takes twenty minutes and a lot of crouching to ask stallholders. His mother finds you first and hugs him so hard he squeaks. She thanks you twice and never asks what you do for a living.

choices.label: Fetch the market warden
choices.res: The warden knows the boy by name and sighs like it isn't the first time. You leave them to it.

events.title: The Rival's Window
events.text: You pass a rival house in daylight. Its front windows are freshly washed, a new sign gleams over the door, and a girl in a very good dress is laughing with a merchant on the step.

choices.label: Take notes on what they're doing right
choices.res: Fresh flowers by the door, a menu card in the window, prices that are only a little higher than yours. You write it all down.

choices.label: Keep walking
choices.res: Not your house, not your problem. Today, anyway.

exLoverOpeners:
She stops dead halfway across the cobbles when she hears your footsteps, staring for two heartbeats before her shoulders drop with a breath she'd clearly been holding. No vow binds her in this new cycle, yet {name} steps right inside your reach as if her feet know the distance by heart.

"I thought you looked familiar from down the street, Sam," she says quietly, fingers brushing your sleeve. "If you need another pair of hands at {house}, keep your coin. Just tell me where my room is."

You find {name} leaning against a tea-stall awning, squinting at your face the moment you round the corner. Something sharp and fond crosses her eyes—an ache that has outlived the world resetting around you.

"Funny," {name} murmurs, folding her arms over her chest to hide a sudden smile. "I don't even have a contract in front of me, and I still walked straight down the road toward {house}. Don't insult me with a signing fee, Sam. Just ask."

{name} slows down the instant your eyes meet, stepping out of the foot traffic to walk alongside you without being asked. Even without old promises tying her to your belt, there is zero distance in the way she falls into step beside your shoulder.

"Starting fresh again, Sam?" she asks softly, looking up through her lashes. "Fine. Keep your gold for the house—if you want me back, you already have me."
exLoverHireRes: {name} slips into step beside you back toward {house}, waving off your purse before you can reach for it. "Already yours once," she murmurs lightly. "Call it an old habit."
goddessExLover: Behind your shoulder, a dry warm voice curls right into your ear: "Oh, wonderful. Not even a signing fee for an old flame? Tell me you aren't collecting the whole set again, Sam."
A faint flicker of amber sparks at your collar as {goddess} mutters in the back of your head: "Free of charge? How terribly generous of her. Don't expect me to clap."
"She remembers that much without the ring?" {goddess} hums low against your ear, sharp-edged and possessive. "Fine. Bring her home. Just remember whose lantern lit your door this morning."
exLoverMemoryTiers:
Halfway across the square, {name} slows to a stop and stares at you for a beat too long, frowning as if a dream slipped out of reach the instant she woke.
